title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: review set limit per case rises from 20 to 100 (Worldwide)
summary: The published limit and roadmap details are supported, but the access boundary is overstated: eDiscovery Administrators can access case data without first becoming case members. The sources also do not explicitly establish the higher limit's rollout default, and the storage-cost paragraph needs to acknowledge Microsoft's separate billing guidance.

claims.claim: A case can contain at most 40 million documents across all its review sets.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Adding content copies the items and their metadata into Microsoft-managed Azure Storage dedicated to the case.
claims.quote: When you add content to a review set, the items and their metadata are copied to a Microsoft-managed Azure Storage location dedicated to the case.

claims.claim: Storage is provisioned per case and shared by review sets in that case.
claims.quote: Storage is provisioned per case. Multiple review sets within the same case share the underlying case storage, with logical separation so each review set's content remains independently queryable, taggable, and exportable.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and storage; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft states that customers do not see, manage or pay directly for review set storage resources.
claims.quote: The storage is Microsoft-owned and Microsoft-managed. Customers don't see, manage, or pay for these storage resources directly.
claims.fix: Keep the quoted storage-resource statement, but add: 'Microsoft's Billing in eDiscovery page separately says that adding non-Microsoft 365 AI data to a review set incurs pay-as-you-go data-storage charges; legacy review-set imports are excluded.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/edisc-billing. Narrow the cost rationale to the higher limit itself rather than implying that every review-set data type is unbilled.

claims.claim: Customers have no direct storage URL or key, and review set content is accessible through the Purview portal and approved export workflows.
claims.quote: There's no customer-accessible SAS token, account key, or storage URL for review set content. Access to review set content is only through the Microsoft Purview portal and approved export workflows.

claims.claim: Access to case content stays limited to case members.
claims.quote: Access case data for any case in the organization. ... Manage any eDiscovery case after they add themselves as a member of the case.
claims.fix: Replace 'Access stays limited to case members' with 'Access is governed by eDiscovery permissions; eDiscovery Administrators can access case data for any case in the organisation, and must add themselves as members to manage a case.' Keep the separate portal/export access statement.

claims.claim: In data-spillage scenarios, removing items from review sets requires deleting the eDiscovery case.
claims.quote: In data spillage scenarios, the only way to remove items in a review set is to delete the eDiscovery case. Other search and purge methods don't remove items from a review set.

claims.quote: An eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all eDiscovery cases, they can audit and oversee all cases and associated compliance searches.
